euro.definition: The basic monetary unit of most members of the European Union (introduced in 1999).

british-pound.definition: The standard currency unit of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is divided into 100 pence.

swiss-franc.definition: The official currency used in Switzerland.

canadian-dollar.definition: The dollar is Canada’s standard unit for measuring and exchanging money.

australian-dollar.definition: The dollar serves as the standard monetary unit in Australia and Nauru.

indian-rupee.definition: The Indian rupee is India’s standard monetary unit, divided into 100 paise.

cash.definition: Prompt payment for goods or services in currency or by check.

credit-card.definition: A plastic or metal payment card from a bank or other lender lets its holder buy goods and services with borrowed money up to a set limit, then repay the balance, usually with interest, an extra charge for borrowing.

debit-card.definition: A payment card that lets you buy goods or withdraw cash using funds taken directly from your bank account.

check.definition: A written order directing a bank to pay money.

wire-transfer.definition: A specified sum transferred between bank accounts through a regulated payment network, such as SWIFT or a national settlement system.

contactless.definition: Operating without touch, as when a card makes a payment or a device takes a measurement remotely.

paypal.definition: To send money to another person using PayPal, an online payment service.

cryptocurrency.definition: A currency based on the usage of cryptography to secure transactions.

receipt.definition: An acknowledgment (usually tangible) that payment has been made.

invoice.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

statement.definition: A message that is stated or declared.

balance.definition: Equality between the totals of the credit and debit sides of an account.

overdraft.definition: A draft in excess of the credit balance.

due-date.definition: In education, it describes work or events scheduled for completion by a particular date, which serves as the deadline.

late-fee.definition: A set of rules for calculating charges after a payment is late, including grace periods, maximum amounts, and higher fees for longer delays.

online-banking.definition: Managing a bank account through internet services, such as checking balances, transferring money, and paying bills, is known as online banking.

mobile-app.definition: A software program built to work on a smartphone or tablet, usually obtained through an app store or another digital platform.

blockchain.definition: A shared digital ledger records transactions in blocks linked by cryptography, creating a chain that network participants maintain and cannot alter.

bitcoin.definition: A digital currency maintained by a shared transaction record and protected by mathematical techniques, allowing direct payments without central control.

nft.definition: A non-fungible token, meaning a unique digital record on a blockchain that can represent ownership or a claim connected with a digital item.
nft.exampleUsage: The technology lesson explains what an NFT record represents.

fintech.definition: Technology used to provide or improve financial services such as payments, banking, or money management.
fintech.exampleUsage: The course examines how fintech has changed digital payments.

peer-to-peer.definition: Describing a system in which people or devices interact directly with one another rather than through a central intermediary.
peer-to-peer.exampleUsage: The app uses a peer-to-peer system for transferring data.

crowdfunding.definition: Funding from a large number of small backers.
